Teradyne invests in Bright Machines to connect robotics and AI hardware testing

The planned collaboration links assembly, inspection, material movement and electrical test data, without a timeline for a fully integrated system.

The Robot Report ↗5 October 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 1Videos 1

Investment accompanies collaboration

Teradyne and Bright Machines announced a strategic investment on October 5 alongside plans to integrate Teradyne robotics and testing technologies with Bright Machines’ manufacturing platform. The target is AI and data-center infrastructure production. The reviewed announcements do not disclose an investment amount, so this is not a funding round with a stated monetary size.

Following each unit through production

Areas under evaluation include precision assembly, robotic loading and unloading of test equipment, and autonomous material movement. Universal Robots cobots, board testers and Bright Machines’ platform would contribute different data streams to a unit’s production history. The aim is to connect design choices with assembly execution and measured electrical performance.

A phased integration effort

Bright Machines told The Robot Report that it had begun adding Universal Robots to its lines and identifying technical integration areas. Work will proceed in phases tied to customer applications and requirements; no complete-system timeline has been announced. Its record of more than 130 microfactory deployments in over 10 countries predates this deal and is not a deployment count for the new collaboration.
